#1
ĐANG HỌC
People often say that honesty is the best policy.
#2
Yet every single person lies.
#3
Some lies are small, others change lives forever.
#4
But have you ever wondered why we lie?
#5
And more importantly, were we born dishonest?
#6
Or did we learn to lie?
#7
Today we explore one of the most fascinating behaviors of the human mind.
#8
A newborn cannot lie.
#9
Babies communicate only through instinct and emotion.
#10
The ability to lie appears much later, usually around the age of two or three.
#11
At this stage, children begin to understand that other people have different thoughts and beliefs.
#12
This discovery changes everything.
#13
For the first time, a child realizes that another person's mind can be influenced.
#14
And that is where lying begins.
#15
Children rarely lie because they are evil.
#16
More often, they lie because they are learning.
#17
A child's first lie is usually not an act of manipulation.
#18
It is an experiment, a way of asking what happens if I say something that isn't true.
#19
Sometimes children lie to avoid punishment.
#20
A broken vase, a spilled glass of milk, chocolate on their face, wet pants.
#21
Instead of admitting what happened, they instinctively searched for an escape.
#22
It wasn't me.
#23
It fell by itself.
#24
I didn't do it.
#25
Not because they enjoy lying, but because they are afraid of the consequences.
#26
Sometimes they lie for a different reason.
#27
They simply want attention.
#28
A child may pretend to have a stomach ache or claim something exciting happened just to bring everyone's eyes back to them.
#29
Other times, they lie out of pure curiosity.
#30
They want to discover how people react and whether words alone can change reality.
#31
Every successful lie teaches the brain a powerful lesson.
#32
My words can change what someone else believes.
#33
That realization is a major milestone in human development.
#34
It marks the moment when language becomes more than a way to describe the world.
#35
It becomes a tool capable of shaping another person's mind as we grow older.
#36
Our lies grow with us.
#37
They become less obvious and far more sophisticated.
#38
We no longer lie just to avoid punishment.
#39
We lie to protect our image, to avoid conflict, to impress others, to hide our fears.
#40
A job applicant exaggerates their experience, hoping to appear more qualified.
#41
A friend says, "I'm fine."
#42
While silently struggling inside, a husband says, "I'm stuck in traffic even though he left work late."
#43
Someone posts smiling vacation photos while feeling lonely and unhappy.
#44
Not every lie is selfish.
#45
Parents create magical stories about Santa Claus to fill childhood with wonder.
#46
A doctor may choose gentle words before delivering painful news.
#47
Sometimes the truth hurts.
#48
Sometimes kindness comes before complete honesty.
#49
Psychologists call these white lies.
#50
Small deceptions meant to protect feelings rather than cause harm.
#51
But every lie, whether kind or selfish, has one thing in common.
#52
It changes what another person believes.
#53
And that is what makes lying such a uniquely human ability.
#54
Can we ever stop lying?
#55
Probably not.
#56
Lying is woven into the fabric of human life.
#57
It protects, it comforts, it manipulates, it inspires.
#58
Every day we decide what to reveal and what to keep hidden.
#59
The real question isn't do we lie.
#60
It's when is a lie justified and when does it become dangerous?
#61
Perhaps understanding why we lie is the first step toward becoming more honest not only with others but with ourselves.
#62
Remember, every action has a reason.
#63
Every choice tells a story and every behavior begins with a why.
#64
Thank you for watching.
#65
If this video made you see yourself differently, leave a like and share your thoughts in the comments.
#66
Subscribe to the Human Why for more videos exploring the psychology behind everyday life.
#67
Until next time, keep asking why.
